fields.v: Inconsistencies: in Table 3 the Avg. row gives 4.8 in the Avg. column, below every per-setting average (4.4-8.1); the mean of the 11 per-model averages is about 7.6 (p. 12); text says the Level 2 E2E advantage 'persisted only for Llama-3.3-70B', but rebuilt Table 3 also gives Phi4-14B E2E L2 6.2 vs Cascade L2 3.1 (p. 11-12); text says Python 'remains dominant among closed-source agents', but Table 5 gives Gemini-2.5-flash JS 17.0 > Python 15.5 (p. 14); ALE gains in text and Table 6 do not all match the before/after values: GPT-5-mini Python→JavaScript 63.2→93.3 is +30.1 but reported +31.1; Gemini Python→Java +16.7 (values give 16.8), Gemma3-27B +3.2 (3.3) and +6.0 (6.1), rounding (p. 14-15); PV similarity metric defined as 'strings cosine similarity' in the text but as Levenshtein distance in Table 2 and the Table 4 caption (p. 10, 13); test points described as cascading ('if the former one fails, the following will never get passed', p. 11; deviations cause complete project failures, p. 17) yet §7.2 says isolated timeout errors 'will not propagate to subsequent test points' (p. 17); Table 6 caption repeats 'Bold emphasizes the difference between ProjectEvalPlus and its peers' (p. 15); 'theoretically proves' support for all languages without a formal proof (p. 9). Table 1, Table 4 and Table 5 open-source rows are jumbled in the extracted text and not used; the Table 3 open-source rows were rebuilt by reading the numbers row by row (6 per model), checked against each row's Avg and the column Avg row; the Table 5 closed-source rows (18 values each) read cleanly. 'LLM agents' are models; no agent framework named. Repository: https://github.com/RyanLoil/ProjectEvalPlus/ (open source). Pre-registration: not claimed. Programming languages: Python, Java, JavaScript (testcodes in Python)
fields.quote: Therefore, the strings cosine similarity is directly used to measure their similarity.
fields.where: §3.3 Evaluation Process, p. 10 (vs Table 2, p. 10, and Table 4 caption, p. 13)
fields.why: Two reporting inconsistencies are missing from Notes: the PV metric is cosine similarity in the text but Levenshtein distance in Tables 2 and 4, and cascading test points are said both to propagate and not to propagate failures.
fields.doubt: O texto da pág. 10 diz que os PV são medidos por similaridade de cosseno, mas a Tabela 2 e a legenda da Tabela 4 dizem distância de Levenshtein. Além disso, a pág. 11 diz que os pontos de teste são em cascata e a §7.2 (pág. 17) diz que erros isolados não se propagam. Decide se juntas estas incoerências às Notas.
